edge: Annotate one of multiple specparams in an expression.
negative: Detect continued use of the preannotation expression value.
positive: Annotate a specparam used in a procedural delay expression and observe the recalculated delay.

edge: Place conditional and unconditional paths with identical terminals in the same specify block.
negative: Provide the same terminals under a different condition and verify that path is not selected.
positive: Apply COND IOPATH to a specify path with the matching condition and terminals.

edge: Compare otherwise equivalent conditional entries with and without RETAIN.
notes: Accept either implementation choice for RETAIN.
positive: Annotate a matching conditional path from COND IOPATH while accepting ignored RETAIN data.

edge: Provide conditional and ifnone paths with the same terminals.
negative: Verify a regular conditional path is not selected in place of ifnone.
positive: Apply CONDELSE IOPATH values to a matching ifnone path.

edge: Compare equivalent CONDELSE entries with and without RETAIN.
notes: Accept either implementation choice for RETAIN.
positive: Annotate an ifnone path while accepting an implementation that ignores RETAIN.

edge: Use syntactically corresponding condition expressions on paths sharing both terminals.
negative: Verify that a path with matching ports but a different condition remains unchanged.
positive: Provide two paths between the same ports with opposite conditions and verify annotation changes only the path matching the SDF COND expression.

edge: Use default invocation settings and verify both limits equal the delay.
notes: Invocation-option spelling is implementation-specific and not part of the oracle.
positive: Annotate delay 5 with configured reject 40% and error 80% and observe limits 2 and 4.

edge: Use a module with no specify paths and verify DEVICE targets all output-driving primitives.
positive: Apply DEVICE to a module having specify paths to multiple outputs and verify all are targeted.

edge: Name an output having no specify path and verify all primitives driving that output are targeted.
negative: Verify specify paths to another output remain unchanged.
positive: Name one module output and verify all specify paths to that output are targeted.

edge: Use a named module instance with no specify paths and verify all primitives driving its outputs are targeted.
negative: Verify paths outside the named module instance remain unchanged.
positive: Name a module instance having specify paths to multiple outputs and verify all such paths are targeted.

edge: Drive through a net connection above the named source.
positive: Place a source above its load and drive from ports at and above the source level.

edge: Mix explicit and empty pulse-limit components in one IOPATH delay tuple.
negative: Detect replacement of a pulse-limit value represented by empty parentheses.
positive: Set pulse limits, then apply an IOPATH with empty pulse-limit fields and verify the existing limits remain.

edge: Exercise both upward and downward annotation directions.
negative: Verify connected ports outside the directional hierarchical subset are unaffected.
positive: Annotate through a port connected across multiple hierarchy levels and observe all connected ports in the annotation direction.

edge: Use a multisource, multiload net with nested overlapping subsets.
negative: Detect one annotation incorrectly replacing the other outside their overlap.
positive: Apply two source-overlapping annotations to nested load ports with different delays and observe each hierarchical subset.

edge: Use a file containing only constructs unrelated to SystemVerilog timing and verify no timing state changes.
positive: Include a TIMINGENV construct alongside valid timing annotation and verify that only the relevant timing annotation affects simulation.

edge: Mix supplied and omitted delay and pulse-limit components in one interconnect annotation.
negative: Detect a missing interconnect component filled differently from the corresponding specify-path rule.
positive: Omit selected interconnect transition-delay or pulse-limit values and verify specify-path filling rules supply them.

edge: Use inout module ports while retaining module ports at both endpoints.
negative: Attempt INTERCONNECT annotation directly between primitive pins and verify no interconnect delay is created.
positive: Annotate delay between connected module ports.

edge: Exercise each allowed inout substitution independently.
negative: Use an input-only source or output-only load and verify it is not accepted as a legal INTERCONNECT pair.
positive: Annotate from an output port to an input port and from an inout port to an inout port.

edge: Use an existing source on a different net and verify the same load fallback.
negative: Detect omission of the load delay merely because the named source mismatches.
positive: Name a missing source on a multisource load net and verify every actual source-to-load path uses the annotated delay.

edge: Exercise missing-source and different-net conditions separately.
negative: Detect silent handling of an existing source and load on different nets.
positive: Name a missing source port and verify that annotation issues a warning.

edge: Use inout ports as one or both legal endpoints.
negative: Verify another source on the same net does not acquire the pair-specific delay.
positive: On a multisource net, annotate one existing source/load pair and verify its distinct delay.

edge: Observe through $display, $monitor, and an expression.
positive: Observe the same signal at source and load and verify undelayed versus delayed transitions.

edge: Use a multisource net.
negative: Detect retention of the earlier source-specific delay.
positive: Apply INTERCONNECT for one source then PORT to the load and verify every source uses the PORT delay.

edge: Assign distinct values to all 12 transition components and both pulse limits for each.
negative: Detect aliasing of pulse limits between two transition components.
positive: Annotate distinct values for multiple interconnect transitions and their reject/error limits and observe the corresponding transition behavior.

edge: Generate a long burst with delay greater than the inter-transition interval so many output events remain pending.
negative: Detect loss of a pending output event caused by a fixed queue-depth limit.
notes: Use a finite stress count; the oracle is absence of an implementation-imposed fixed schedule-count limit, not proof over an actually infinite run.
positive: Create several input transitions whose delayed interconnect output events are simultaneously pending and verify none is discarded merely due to a schedule-count limit.

edge: Target a conditional specify path.
negative: Use unmatched IOPATH terminals and verify a different path is not modified.
positive: Apply IOPATH delay values to a matching nonconditional specify path.

edge: Compare annotation of equivalent IOPATH entries with and without RETAIN.
notes: This is an explicit implementation permission; a case must accept both supported RETAIN behavior and ignored RETAIN data.
positive: Annotate an IOPATH containing RETAIN and accept an implementation that applies the path delay while ignoring RETAIN.

edge: Provide conditional and unconditional paths with the same terminals and verify condition-sensitive matching.
negative: Use an IOPATH with a mismatched terminal name or condition and verify it does not alter that path.
positive: Annotate an IOPATH whose terminal names and condition match a specify path.

edge: Provide otherwise identical conditional checks and select one by its condition.
negative: Change only the timing-check type or condition and verify the nonmatching check is not annotated.
positive: Annotate a timing check with matching type, terminals, and condition.

edge: Annotate disjoint and overlapping values from separate files.
positive: Call $sdf_annotate twice for the same timing item and verify second-file INCREMENT and ABSOLUTE behavior.

edge: Exercise exact zero and independently underflow reject and error limits.
negative: Detect a negative resulting reject or error limit.
positive: Increment an existing pulse limit by a larger negative value and verify the result is zero.

edge: Contrast an output port with a connected net target.
negative: Attempt to target an output-only module port and verify it is not accepted as a NETDELAY target.
positive: Annotate NETDELAY to an input port, an inout port, and a net.

edge: Use multiple sources and multiple load ports on the same target net.
negative: Detect application of the delay to only one source on the target net.
positive: Target a multisource net and verify transitions from each source to an annotated load use the NETDELAY value.

edge: Mix input and inout load ports on the targeted net.
negative: Verify a load port on another net remains unchanged.
positive: Target a net with multiple load ports and verify every connected load receives the delay.

edge: Target an inout module port directly.
negative: Verify another load port is not selected merely because a direct port target was named.
positive: Target an input module port and verify that port receives the NETDELAY interconnect delay.

edge: Combine unrelated constructs with a separately unannotatable SystemVerilog timing item and distinguish the required warning for the latter.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording; isolate warning provenance where possible.
positive: Annotate an SDF file containing a TIMINGENV construct and verify that the unrelated construct produces no warning.

edge: Mix conditional and nonconditional paths between the same terminals and verify all are annotated.
negative: Include a path with a different source or destination and verify it remains unchanged.
positive: Provide two oppositely conditioned specify paths between the named ports and verify an unconditional IOPATH annotates both.

edge: Apply after an existing IOPATH delay annotation.
negative: Detect a path-delay change caused solely by PATHPULSE.
positive: Apply each construct to a path and verify pulse limits change while delay remains fixed.

edge: Test reject and error limits around the delay boundary.
positive: Compare pulse behavior for PATHPULSE limits equal to and greater than the delay.

edge: Apply PATHPULSE to a matching conditional specify path.
positive: Apply PATHPULSE to a matching nonconditional specify path pulse limit.

edge: Use a conditional specify path as the target.
positive: Apply PATHPULSEPERCENT to a matching specify path and observe the percentage-derived pulse limit.

edge: Compare single-source and multisource nets.
negative: Name an unrelated port and verify the intended load is unchanged.
positive: Apply PORT to a load on a multisource net and verify each source-to-load propagation uses the delay.

edge: Use distinct delays for easy source-specific observation.
positive: On a three-source net, apply PORT then INTERCONNECT for one source and verify only that source/load delay changes.

edge: Require both an edge and a logical condition to match.
negative: Provide otherwise corresponding negedge and unqualified checks and verify they remain unchanged.
positive: Use a posedge-qualified SDF check and verify it annotates the corresponding posedge SystemVerilog check.

edge: Select boundary indices of an instance array in separate annotations.
negative: Verify another array element remains unchanged.
positive: Select one indexed element of an instance array and verify annotation is confined to that element.

edge: Use a file containing both successful and unannotatable data and count entries only as defined for individual annotations.
negative: Detect a successfully annotated item missing from the log.
notes: Do not depend on entry wording.
positive: Annotate multiple timing items with log_file specified and verify one entry for each.

edge: Use the same relative SDF instance paths under two different selected scopes.
negative: Verify a sibling outside the selected hierarchy remains unchanged.
positive: Select one of two sibling instances and verify annotation is confined to the selected hierarchy.

edge: Place identical child instance names beneath the caller and a sibling to distinguish the default scope.
negative: Verify an equivalent hierarchy outside the caller module is unchanged.
positive: Call $sdf_annotate with module_instance omitted and verify relative SDF paths resolve under the caller module.

edge: Provide all seven argument positions.
negative: Supply arguments out of order or more than the grammar permits.
positive: Call $sdf_annotate with only sdf_file and with selected later arguments using empty slots.

edge: Use distinct values to verify ordering.
negative: Verify a nonmatching timing-check type is unchanged.
positive: Apply distinct BIDIRECTSKEW values to a matching $fullskew check.

edge: Apply PATHPULSE followed by IOPATH to shared pulse-limit components; compare INCREMENT and ABSOLUTE.
positive: Apply distinct earlier and later ABSOLUTE annotations to the same timing components and observe the later values.

edge: Compare one-value and twelve-value forms.
positive: Supply each supported delay tuple length with distinct values and observe v1 for 0-to-1.

edge: Compare six-value derived mapping with explicit v7 in twelve-value form.
positive: Choose unequal v1 and v3 and verify their minimum for three- and six-value forms.

edge: Compare two-value and three-value forms.
positive: Observe 0-to-z with distinct tuple values across supported lengths.

edge: Compare one-value and two-value forms.
positive: Use distinct v1 and v2 and observe the selected 1-to-0 delay.

edge: Exercise all tuple lengths.
positive: Use unequal component values to verify each minimum.

edge: Exercise all tuple lengths.
positive: Use distinct values for each supported tuple length and observe 1-to-z.

edge: Compare three- and six-value forms.
positive: Use unequal v2 and v6 to verify max selection.

edge: Compare six- and twelve-value forms.
positive: Use unequal v1 and v4 to verify max selection.

edge: Exercise all tuple lengths.
positive: Use unequal values to verify each maximum.

edge: Compare three-value and six-value forms.
positive: Observe z-to-0 with distinct values across tuple lengths.

edge: Compare the tuple-length boundary.
positive: Observe z-to-1 using distinct values in three- and six-value forms.

edge: Compare three- and six-value forms.
positive: Use unequal values to verify each minimum.

edge: Use a direct string literal.
negative: Pass an expression of an unsupported nonintegral, nonstring type.
positive: Pass a string variable naming an SDF file and separately an integral packed character string.

edge: Verify the setup component remains unchanged.
positive: Apply HOLD to matching $hold and $setuphold checks.

edge: Use inout ports.
negative: Use a nonmatching source/load pair and verify another connection is unchanged.
positive: Apply INTERCONNECT between connected module output and input ports and observe delayed propagation.

edge: Annotate multiple specparams.
negative: Verify an unrelated specparam is unchanged.
positive: Use LABEL to replace a named specparam value and observe behavior controlled by it.

edge: Exercise each deterministic explicit keyword against a different configuration selection.
negative: Detect use of the configuration-file member instead of the explicit argument.
positive: Set configuration MTM_SPEC to MAXIMUM and explicit mtm_spec to TYPICAL, then verify the typical member is annotated.

edge: Omit mtm_spec and accept whichever member the simulator selects under default TOOL_CONTROL.
negative: Detect selection of a different triple member under a deterministic keyword.
notes: TOOL_CONTROL does not prescribe which member the simulator selects.
positive: Annotate a distinct min:typ:max triple under MAXIMUM, MINIMUM, and TYPICAL and verify the selected member.

edge: Distinguish version-scoped NETDELAY from constructs available in other SDF versions.
notes: Materialization requires an SDF reader mode supporting one of the listed versions.
positive: Apply NETDELAY from a listed SDF version to a legal module-port target and separately to a net target.

edge: Use distinct values to verify ordering.
positive: Apply distinct NOCHANGE values to a matching $nochange check.

negative: Verify another timing-check type is unchanged.
positive: Apply PERIOD to a matching $period check and observe the new limit.

edge: Target an inout load port.
positive: Apply a PORT delay to a module input load and observe delayed propagation.

edge: Verify removal remains unchanged.
positive: Apply RECOVERY to matching $recovery and $recrem checks.

edge: Verify component ordering.
positive: Apply distinct values to each supported check form.

edge: Verify recovery remains unchanged.
positive: Apply REMOVAL to matching $removal and $recrem checks.

edge: Omit scale_factors and verify unity scaling.
negative: Detect swapping of minimum, typical, and maximum factor positions.
positive: Use distinct factors with distinct min/typ/max values and verify each corresponding product.

edge: Use unity explicit factors against nonunity configuration factors.
negative: Detect use of configuration factors instead of the explicit argument.
positive: Provide explicit factors that differ from configuration SCALE_FACTORS and verify the explicit products.

edge: Exercise each explicit scale_type against a different configuration mode.
negative: Detect use of the configuration SCALE_TYPE instead of the explicit argument.
positive: Supply scale_type conflicting with configuration and verify the explicit mode controls scaling.

edge: Omit scale_type and verify FROM_MTM correspondence.
negative: Select FROM_MAXIMUM and detect factors applied from another triple member.
positive: Use a distinct min:typ:max triple and distinct factors to distinguish all four scale modes.

edge: Verify the $setuphold hold component remains unchanged.
positive: Apply SETUP to matching $setup and $setuphold checks.

edge: Verify component ordering.
positive: Apply distinct v1 and v2 values to each supported matching check form.

negative: Verify another timing-check type is not annotated.
positive: Apply SKEW to matching $skew and $timeskew checks.

edge: Mix annotatable and unannotatable relevant data and isolate warning presence for the latter.
negative: Detect silent failure to annotate relevant SDF timing data.
notes: The oracle is warning presence, not diagnostic wording or one-warning-per-item grouping.
positive: Provide relevant SDF timing data that cannot be applied to the selected design object and verify warning presence.

edge: Verify the second $width limit remains unchanged.
positive: Apply WIDTH to a matching $width check.

edge: Exercise both upward and downward source-port directions.
negative: Verify sources outside the directional hierarchical subset do not acquire that source-port annotation.
positive: Annotate from a source port with connected sources beyond it in the annotation direction and verify each source uses the annotation.

edge: Compare three- and four-or-more-value inputs.
positive: Supply more than three distinct SDF values to a three-delay construct and verify extras have no effect.

edge: Use tied minima.
positive: Use three unequal delays and observe the minimum for transition to X.

edge: Mix qualified and unqualified corresponding checks.
negative: Include a check with different signal names and verify it is not selected merely because qualifiers are absent.
positive: Use an unqualified SDF SETUPHOLD and corresponding SystemVerilog checks with posedge, negedge, edge, and conditional event forms; verify all are annotated.

edge: Use an SDF file that supplies no value for the observed timing item.
negative: Backannotate an SDF file omitting an existing specify timing value and detect any modification of that value.
positive: Annotate one of two existing timing values and verify that the omitted value retains its prior value.

edge: Observe both a port and a net connection above the load.
positive: Place a load above its source and observe equal delay at ports above the load.
